summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a two-day history of worsening epigastric and mid-abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting, following a recent gastric bypass reversal. She was managed conservatively with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV pain control. A CT scan revealed significant inflammatory changes near the gastrogastric anastomosis, prompting initiation of ciprofloxacin and metronidazole. Her G-tube was initially placed to gravity drainage for symptom relief. Due to a malfunctioning and leaking G-tube, she underwent a successful exchange to a new 18 French MIC tube under fluoroscopic guidance. After the exchange, she tolerated advancement to a bariatric stage 5 diet, with marked improvement in pain and nausea. She was transitioned to oral pain medications, remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable, and was discharged home on a 10-day course of antibiotics with follow-up instructions. Her mental status remained clear, and she was ambulating independently at discharge.
problems: Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
